strengths: Introduces a large-scale 3D/2D affordance grounding dataset, Affogato, with 150K objects and 750K open-vocabulary query-heatmap pairs, substantially surpassing prior datasets in scale and diversity.

The Affogato-Engine pipeline is well motivated and described: it uses foundation models (Gemma3, Molmo, SAM) with multi-view rendering, point prompting, mask generation, and voting-based 3D heatmap aggregation to automatically produce annotations at scale.

The paper provides simple but effective baselines (Espresso-3D and Espresso-2D) and demonstrates that training with Affogato improves in-domain performance, cross-dataset robustness, cross-category open-vocabulary generalization, and 2D transfer to AGD20K.

Includes human quality evaluation of 5K query-heatmap pairs, test-split refinement, failure-mode analysis, dataset statistics, and multiple ablations/qualitative results, showing awareness of dataset quality issues.
Tackles an important and challenging problem in visual affordance grounding, with potential impact for embodied AI, robotics, and human-object interaction understanding.
The paper is clearly written and organized, with extensive experiments spanning 3D and 2D settings, zero-shot evaluation, cross-domain transfer, and partial-view evaluation.
weaknesses: Annotation quality is validated on only 1K objects / 5K pairs, and 15.4% of evaluated pairs were rated 'not good' before refinement; it is unclear how many noisy annotations remain in the full training set after refinement, which may weaken the benchmark and learned models.

The test split is human-verified/refined while the training portion appears to remain automatically generated, creating a potential distribution mismatch and possibly inflating benchmark scores; the paper does not ablate training with only refined annotations.

The Espresso model architecture is intentionally simple and largely assembled from frozen pretrained encoders and existing decoder designs, so the algorithmic novelty is limited and the main contribution rests on the dataset/pipeline.
No evaluation is reported on the Affogato 2D benchmark itself; the 2D dataset is used for pretraining and evaluated only on AGD20K, leaving the quality and utility of Affogato's 2D split unverified.

Potential overlap or leakage between Objaverse and source datasets such as PartNet/3D-AffordanceNet is not discussed, and the test split separation is described at the pair level rather than clearly at the object level.

Absolute 3D grounding performance remains modest in several settings (e.g., aIoU around 0.14-0.20 on Affogato), and MAE is acknowledged to be unreliable, so practical affordance-grounding capability is not fully demonstrated.

The paper relies heavily on generated natural-language queries, but provides limited analysis of query diversity, bias, or whether the 'open-vocabulary' supervision is systematically different from closed-vocabulary alternatives.

Minor presentation/citation issues exist (e.g., Figure A2 refers to 3D-AffordanceNet as [36], which appears to be a different reference), and dataset release/licensing details are not visible in the main paper.

strengths: Introduces a very large-scale 3D/2D affordance grounding dataset (150K objects, 750K query-heatmap pairs), far exceeding prior datasets in scale and object/affordance diversity.
The automated multi-stage pipeline is clearly described and uses strong foundation models (Gemma3, Molmo, SAM) with multi-view aggregation, making the dataset construction scalable.
Includes a human quality assessment of a subset and constructs a refined test split, showing some effort toward benchmark reliability.
Experiments suggest that pretraining on Affogato improves cross-dataset generalization to LASO and zero-shot performance on AGD20K compared with prior baselines.
Provides a simple unified Espresso baseline for both 3D and 2D affordance grounding with frozen foundation features and a text-conditioned decoder.
weaknesses: The benchmark ground truth is mostly model-generated rather than human-verified. Only 1K objects / 5K pairs were evaluated, with 15.4% rated 'not good' and 12.3% only 'ok'; only test-split failures were refined, leaving training labels noisy and undermining claims of high-quality supervision.

Evaluation on Affogato may be biased toward the generation pipeline itself, since models are trained on the same automatically generated supervision. Absolute performance is low (e.g., best aIoU 0.136 in Table 2), raising doubts about annotation reliability and the usefulness of the benchmark.
The 2D Affogato dataset/test split is not actually evaluated. All 2D experiments are on AGD20K, so the proposed 2D benchmark component remains unvalidated.

Open-vocabulary and cross-domain claims are weakened because queries are LLM-generated in both training and evaluation. There is no human-written query benchmark, and potential object-class overlap between Affogato pretraining and AGD20K 'unseen' classes is not analyzed.
The diversity/coverage metrics in Table 3d may reward spatially spread or noisy heatmaps rather than genuinely meaningful affordance diversity; no human correlation is provided.

Technical novelty is limited: the pipeline relies heavily on off-the-shelf foundation models, and Espresso is a thin decoder over frozen features. The paper reads more as a dataset construction report than a rigorous benchmark/algorithmic contribution.

Key methodological details are insufficient for reproducibility: it is unclear how refined 3D test heatmaps are obtained from 2D human refinements, the human evaluation protocol (annotator selection, inter-rater agreement, instructions) is vague, and the dataset link is absent in the supplied PDF.

The comparison with prior datasets is not fully fair or complete: annotation protocols differ, some metrics are not normalized (MAE issues are acknowledged), and training on Affogato substantially hurts in-domain LASO performance relative to training on LASO, a trade-off that is not adequately discussed.

strengths: Introduces Affogato, a large-scale open-vocabulary affordance grounding dataset with 150K 3D object instances and 750K query-heatmap pairs, substantially surpassing prior 3D and 2D affordance datasets in scale and diversity.
Provides both 3D heatmap annotations and projected 2D heatmaps, enabling unified evaluation across 3D point clouds and 2D images from a single dataset.
Proposes an automated multi-stage Affogato-Engine pipeline leveraging Gemma3, Molmo, and SAM with multi-view aggregation, making large-scale annotation feasible and reproducible.
Includes human verification and refinement of the test split, which improves benchmark reliability despite the automated training data.
Demonstrates strong cross-dataset and open-vocabulary generalization: models pretrained on Affogato transfer better to LASO and AGD20K than models trained on prior datasets.

The lightweight Espresso baselines are simple but effective, and the experiments are broad, covering 3D/2D grounding, zero-shot/few-shot/full supervision, cross-category splits, partial views, and qualitative failure modes.
Clearly documents implementation details, computational resources, and failure modes, which supports reproducibility and honest assessment.
weaknesses: The training annotations are automatically generated by foundation models and may contain systematic errors or biases from Gemma3, Molmo, and SAM. Human evaluation reports only 72.3% 'good' annotations and 15.4% 'not good', suggesting non-negligible label noise in the training set.

The dataset is built exclusively on Objaverse synthetic 3D assets without real scene context or background geometry. Although 2D background augmentation is used, real-world, scene-level affordance grounding remains insufficiently validated.

The open-vocabulary queries are generated by a single VLM conditioned on rendered views, which may overrepresent common affordances and miss valid but less typical interaction descriptions, limiting true open-vocabulary coverage.
The human-refined test split is relatively small (5K pairs from 1K objects) compared with the full 750K-pair dataset, so benchmark quality may not fully reflect the quality of the training data.

The Espresso models are intentionally minimal and use frozen pretrained backbones; they are adequate as baselines but do not provide strong algorithmic novelty, and stronger task-specific baselines could change the empirical picture.

Some metrics, especially MAE, are sensitive to annotation scale and cross-dataset normalization, making certain cross-dataset comparisons less reliable; the paper acknowledges this but still reports MAE prominently.
Affordance is represented only as a static heatmap over an object and does not model pose, force, or interaction dynamics, which the paper itself notes as a limitation for embodied agents.

The evaluation focuses on single-object affordance grounding rather than full scene understanding, so the practical impact for real-world agents that interact with multiple objects and contexts is not fully demonstrated.
